# New Local SEO Client Workflow

Get access to their website and their GBP. The onboarding email asks them this. You just have to make sure it’s working.

Dump them in Leadsnap, run a heatmap thing. Get a sense of where they are now. A starting point. This will come in handy later.

We will do this in 2 stages. Basic \+ Advanced. You can skip the steps mentioned as **ADVANCED** in your first run through for a client.   
   
To do list on our end for each pillar of the local SEO process:

# Benchmarking \+ Checking For Obvious Flaws

**To do:**  
Run a heatmap so we have a benchmark. Check the number of reviews for the top 10, the number of photos and see if there are any obvious blackhat scammers in there.

**Explanation:**  
go to [https://app.leadsnap.com/](https://app.leadsnap.com/). Run a heatmap on their main keyword. It will look something like this:

![][image1]

This gives us a place to stand. This biz has a pretty good ranking by the way, usually it’s all red, like this:

![][image2]

Leadsnap also shows you the number of photos and reviews for the top ranking people. These are all factors, if our client is way behind we need to tell them to get their butts in gear and get us reviews \+ photos.![][image3]

Now you have a sense of where they are. Here’s a few things to check that are usually signs of being able to win easily enough:

# Google Business Profile Checks For Easy Wins

Couple things to check for in the GBP.

# Website Checks For Easy Wins

## NAP visible and matching GBP

Make sure that the page shows your business name, your address and your phone number and that it matches what you wrote in the GBP.

## Title \+ H1 match primary category \+ city

Go to the website and find the title. Easiest way is just to hover over the tab in your browser and it will show you the title. Like this:

![][image4]

For a local business we want to see our main keyword in the title tag and the city. If that’s not there \- that’s an easy win

## Number of indexed pages

First thing that I’d like you to do is run a site: google search for your potential client.

So let’s say my client is [profresults.com](http://profresults.com). Go to [google.com](http://google.com), run site:[profresults.com](http://profresults.com) as a search. Go to the tools and it’ll tell you how many pages are indexed:

![][image5] 

We want to have AT LEAST 30 pages indexed. Probably more, but that depends on the competition. But bare minimum is 30\. Just keep that in mind.

## Schema markup

Go to [https://validator.schema.org/](https://validator.schema.org/) and put the website in there. It’ll tell you if they have local business schema in there. If not \- easy win.

## Google embed map

# Fixing The Google Business Profile

## Choose the MAIN keyword you want to rank for

First thing we do is figure out the term we want to rank for. Usually this is obvious. If it’s a plumber in Springfield we probably want to rank for “plumber Springfield”, obviously. If it’s not obvious you can always use AI to figure it out and then double check with your client if you got it right.

Leadsnap also tells you the search volume and competitiveness of keywords. Comes in handy. 

## Competitive analysis in GMB Everywhere

Dump the keyword in GMB everywhere and run a local scan. It will look something like this:   
![][image6]

Now go to the interface of Google My Business. If we have access to their biz it will look something like this:

![][image7]

Click on EDIT PROFILE and let’s go through this step by step:

## Business Name

Make sure it corresponds with their real life biz name. If they have certain keywords in there \- that’s OK. Leave it. But don’t mess around with this if you can help it. 

**Explanation**:  
There’s some things we can do here but we will ONLY mess with this if we have exhausted our other options. For now \- don’t even worry about it.

## Business Category

Limit it to the absolute necessity, 1 main category, anywhere between 0-3 sub categories. 

**Explanation**:  
One of the most important ranking factors. Almost every single time you want to limit this to 1-3 categories. No more. Check GMB everywhere and you’ll usually see that the average number of categories for the top 20 is around 2\. 

This client has 3 categories now. Surveyor, property surveyor, property valuer.![][image8]

If they overlap too much? It dilutes our ranking power.  
If they differ too much and sort of moves away from what we actually do? It dilutes our ranking power.

Check out this analysis you got from GMB everywhere

![][image9]

Most people in the top 10 have just one category. Since surveyor and property surveyor don’t differ much I’m going to nuke property surveyor. I’m also getting rid of ‘valuer’ because it’s not what we’re trying to rank for. 

## Completing The Profile

Complete the profile options as much as you can. We need to get that little green circle next to biz name fully green. Like this:

![][image10]

Explanation:  
Check this out:

![][image11]![][image12]

GMB everywhere does a good job at showing you things that might matter. As you can see, for example, most businesses in the top 10 have zero attributes. This tells you that there’s little correlation between attributes and ranking. 

19/20 businesses in the top 20 have at least 3 out of 5 Profile features. This tells you you might want to do the same. Bare minimum is 3 out of 5\. Full address, website, phone number. Easy way to get to 4 is to click online appointments and link the ‘contact us’ page. 

## Services

Add a full list of services, have AI remove duplicates, add all of them (max 99\) to the Google Business Profile, have AI write a text blurb of max 300 characters for the top 20\.

**Explanation**  
Services are a big deal. Check this example out:

![][image13] 

Average in this top 20 has almost THIRTY services listed. We have 350 unique services just in this top 20\.

The limit for services is 99\. What we want to do is compile a list of services to make sure that Google has as much info as possible AND to make sure that we rank for a wide variety of longtail keywords.

Right now this is what the services list looks like for this example:

![][image14]

Here’s what we do.

(not sure if this is a paid tool, I’ll start with this and leave the other option here as well in case you need it)

### Use Google manually

![][image16]the original Google query and we go over the top 10 people ranking:

![][image17]

We click on each one, copy their services and dump it into one big text document

![][image18]

You end up with a big list like this

![][image19]

New go to whatever AI you use. I use Grok.

Use this prompt:

***I'm pasting a list of services from competitors.*** 

***Your task:***   
***1\. Remove all exact duplicates***   
***2\. Remove all near-identical variants of the same term. Keep only ONE version of each — choose the most common or professional form, but do NOT edit or reword it beyond selecting one from the list.***  
***3\. Do NOT add, remove, combine, rephrase, or limit characters in any way.***   
***4\. Do NOT group, categorize, or format — just output the final clean list, one service per line, nothing else.***

***List:***  
***\[PASTE YOUR LIST HERE\]***

Usually you will still have to go through the list and prune some stuff. You can also prioritize by search traffic. 

If you’re unsure about any services on the list you can always ask the client to tell you if he provides these.

# Onpage SEO

Almost everyone messes this up utterly and completely. All of this stuff takes about an hour once you know what you’re doing. And for the vast majority of businesses this will be enough to make a major difference in ranking.

## Basic (First Run)

### Title tag:

**To do:** 

change title tag into: BEST \+ Primary category \+ cityname \+ primary services \+ near me (if you have space)  
Change H1 primary category \+ cityname  
Change H2 into prominent services  
Add NAP in Footer

**Explanation:**  
If you want to figure out how to change the title tag and you have access to a platform you haven’t messed around with before, just use AI for tech stuff:

![][image25]

Simple.

Anyway \- title tags. Most SEO dudes tell you that you should limit your title to 60 characters. This is horseshit. So let’s inject this thing with trenbolone.

BEST \+ Primary category \+ cityname \+ business name \+ primary services \+ near me (if you have space)

Let’s aim for 200ish characters max

Example:

**BEST Physiotherapist Portsmouth \- if you’re looking for Physiotherapy Services near me or Sports Injuries & Sports Massage near me \- Hope Physiotherapy is the place to be**

### H1:

**To do:** 

H1 \= primary category \+ cityname

H2 lists secondary categories \+ most pertinent services (you find this out while doing research with gmbeverywhere)

**explanation:**

### NAP

NAME ADDRESS PHONE NUMBER \= NAP  
NAP Consistency on Homepage (or GBP landing page) \+ Footer throughout  
GBP embedded map on homepage

## Advanced

### Add Schema

[https://technicalseo.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/](https://technicalseo.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/)

### Build Out The Page Count Like A G

More advanced on page SEO \-\> content related. Usually not necessary, but if you can’t crack top 3 in a few weeks, do this:

Every service gets its own page. So you put together an article on ‘tree sump removal Springfield’, ‘tree cutting Springfield’. 1500 \- 2500 words. Interlinked.

Hierarchy:

RANK 1: Landing page  
RANK 2: category page \- sub category (if applicable) \- Core service 1 \- Core service 2 \- Core service 3  
RANK 3: separate page for remaining services, linked from rank 2\. They interlink amongst each other

So the goal with building out pages is building out topical and local authority. 

Let’s talk about Topical first

### Proving Topical authority

Topical \= expertise on the topic. So if I run a skincare clinic I’d talk about stuff like

\- botox   
\- peeling  
\- microneedling  
\- acne treatment  
\- scar tissue

These are topics related to my field. If you want to know which topics make sense you can easily do it by just googling the term, looking at some competitors, figuring out what they talk about. Can also ask AI, but start by googling on your own. You’re a human, you’re better at figuring out what humans look for than AI. AI should be a failstop.

That’s topical authority. So if you run a skincare place you’d want to speak about ALL of these topics. And that means we’re making subpages.

The structure would be

Skincare clinic  
Skincare clinic \- treatments  
Skincare clinic \- treatments \- botox

Do you see how this makes sense from both a logical human perspective AND a search engine perspective?

So we’re going to set this up. Let’s say your client has 5 main services he sells, that means we’ll be creating 6 pages. skincare clinic/services \+ skincareclinic/services/service1, service2, etc.

Every subpage needs to have between 1000-2000 words of copy. It should be unique copy. It’s easy to use AI to generate this. Just prompt it and make it specific. 

*You are an experienced local SEO copywriter who specializes in \<TYPE OF BUSINESS\> businesses. You write engaging, trustworthy content that ranks well and actually gets read by real people.*

*Task: Create a high-value services page (1,800–2,500 words) to build topical authority around the core topic: "WRITE THE TOPIC HERE. FOR EXAMPLE \- SERVICES THAT OUR SKINCARE CLINIC IN LOCATION OFFERS".*

*Target audience: \<PUT YOUR TARGET AUDIENCE HERE.*

*Search intent: Primarily informational with some commercial – people want to discover the best options, different services, find top local recommendations, get practical tips.*

*Primary keyword: "PRIMARY KEYWORD HERE"*

*Secondary / related keywords to include naturally: IF YOU HAVE THEM, LIST SECONDARY KEYWORDS HERE.* 

*Instructions:*  
*1\. Start with a short summary of search intent and why this page will satisfy it better than competitors.*  
*2\. Build a clear, scannable outline (H1–H3) that covers the topic logically: intro → key concepts → local scene → recommendations → tips → FAQs.*  
*3\. Show expertise (E-E-A-T): Include practical insights, mention real local spots/entities, and add unique tips or a simple checklist.*  
*4\. Structure the article:*  
   *\- Hook \+ promise in the intro*  
   *\- Main sections with short paragraphs, bullets, numbered lists, and 1–2 small tables*  
   *\- Internal linking: Suggest 4–7 natural places to link to supporting pages with example anchor text*  
   *\- FAQ section (6–10 common questions)*  
   *\- Friendly conclusion \+ CTA (visit us, explore menu, etc.)*  
*5\. Tone: Warm, expert but approachable, conversational – like chatting with a knowledgeable expert. Human-sounding, no fluff or repetition.*  
*6\. At the end, add:*  
   *\- Suggested SEO title (60–120 chars)*  
   *\- Meta description (150–160 chars)*  
   *\- H1 suggestion*  
   *\- 3–4 image alt text ideas (local-flavored)*  
   *\- Brief LocalBusiness or FAQ schema outline*

*Output format:*  
*\#\# Quick Strategy Summary*  
*\#\# Outline*  
*\#\# Full Article*  
*\#\# SEO Elements*

This should settle things quite well. 

Then you populate each page with the copy, add some pictures, then we move on to local authority.

### Proving Local authority

Next we have to prove we actually work in the area. This means we add something like: “Areas we serve” in the navigational section. 

You’ll probably need some client input for this if you’re unfamiliar with their exact area. 

Let’s say we pick 5 areas to begin with. Could be neighborhoods, could be areas, towns, doesn’t really matter, you get the picture. 

What we want to do is make a: “areas that we serve” page and link to it from the navigation. We also want to make a subpage for each area. 

Skincare clinic  
Skincare clinic \- areasweserve  
Skincare clinic \- areasweserve \- area1

Here’s a solid prompt for a hyperlocal topical authority page. You’re obviously supposed to substitute the capital letter parts with your stuff:

*You are a senior local SEO specialist who has ranked dozens of single-location businesses in competitive cities like Amsterdam by creating hyperlocal landing pages that dominate neighborhood-specific searches.*

*Task: Write a high-converting, SEO-optimized neighborhood landing page (1,200–2,200 words) for our \<type of business\> "BUSINESS NAME" located in LOCATION and serving \[AREA1\].*

*Page goal: Rank for queries like "\[service\] \[neighborhood\]", "best \[service\] in \[neighborhood\]", "\[service\] near \[landmark\]".*

*Primary keyword: "\[e.g., PRIMARY KEYWORD\]"*

*Key business facts to weave in naturally:*  
*\- Physical address: \[FULL NAP HERE\]*  
*\- Distance/proximity:*   
*\- Unique selling points: \[LIST ANY UNIQUE SELLING POINTS YOUR CLIENT HAS, LIKE organic single-origin beans, in-house roasted, vegan options, outdoor seating with canal views, weekly tastings\]*  
*\- Local tie-ins: Mention neighborhood-specific landmarks, events, pain points (e.g., busy market mornings, tourist crowds, need for quiet work spots)*

*Instructions:*  
*1\. First, analyze hyperlocal intent: What do searchers in this neighborhood really want? How can we prove relevance without claiming a fake address?*  
*2\. Create a scannable outline (H1–H3) that feels local-first: neighborhood intro → why we're perfect for locals here → services/products tailored to area → directions/proof → FAQs → CTA.*  
*3\. Build local authority & E-E-A-T:*  
   *\- Use real neighborhood references (streets, markets, events, history)*  
   *\- Include proximity proof \+ Google Maps embed suggestion*  
   *\- Mention local customer types/stories*  
   *\- Add 2025–2026 relevant local stats or trends if natural*  
*4\. Structure:*  
   *\- Compelling H1 \+ introduction with local hook*  
   *\- Sections on tailored offerings (menu highlights, events, vegan options)*  
   *\- "Why Locals Choose Us" with bullets or mini-testimonials*  
   *\- Directions \+ transport tips from key local spots*  
   *\- Embedded map \+ "Get Directions" CTA suggestion*  
   *\- 8–10 local-flavored FAQs (e.g., "Do you have bike parking in Jordaan?")*  
   *\- Strong CTA: visit, book tasting, view menu*  
*5\. On-page SEO at the end:*  
   *\- SEO title & meta description (hyperlocal \+ compelling)*  
   *\- Suggested schema: LocalBusiness \+ areaServed including neighborhood*  
   *\- 4–6 image alt texts with local keywords*  
   *\- Internal linking: 5–7 suggestions to services, menu, blog, other neighborhoods*  
*6\. Tone: Warm, community-oriented, expert but neighborly. Human, trustworthy voice — no generic corporate speak.*

*Output format:*  
*\#\# Hyperlocal Intent Analysis*  
*\#\# Page Outline*  
*\#\# Full Page Content*  
*\#\# On-Page SEO & Schema Recommendations*

You repeat this for every page. 

In this example we’ve created about 12 new pages. All of it is extremely topical and local. This will help massively in ranking. We just need to connect the pages to make sure Google indexes all of them.

### Interlinking

We’re going to connect our Service Pages and Area Pages so Google understands the business offers different services in different areas. This will make it easier for visitors to find stuff AND the website looks WAY stronger to search engines.

**Important rule**  
Only add links that help the reader. If the link does not make sense for the person reading the page, do not add it.

**Step 1:** Make a quick list (planning)  

Write down all service pages (example: “Plumbing Repair”, “Bathroom Remodel”).    
Write down all area pages (example: “Downtown”, “North Side”, “West Suburbs”).    
Decide which services make sense for which areas.

You only need a simple list or drawing on paper. 

Example:  Plumbing Repair → Downtown, North Side  

Downtown page → Plumbing Repair, Emergency Service

**Step 2:** Where to put the links

On service pages (example: Plumbing Repair page) 

Write 1-3 short sentences in the text that mention an area. Add a link to the area page.

Example: “We help many customers in Downtown.” → link to Downtown page    
At the bottom of the page add a small list: “We also serve these areas” with 3-5 area links.

On area pages (example: Downtown page)  Write 2-4 short sentences in the text that mention a service. Add a link to the service page.  
Example: “Need a fast repair? See our Plumbing Repair service.” → link to Plumbing Repair page.  
    
In the middle or near the bottom add a section called “Services we offer here” with 3-5 service links.

On the homepage and contact page add a small section called “Areas we serve” with links to all area pages.  
    
Add a small section called “Our main services” with links to the most important service pages.

**Step 3:** How to write the link text (anchor text)

Use normal words that a real person would say. Examples:  “our plumbing repair service”    
“services in Downtown”    
“emergency help near you”    
“see bathroom remodel options”

Do not use the same words every time. Change them a little.

**Step 4:** Quick checklist for each page 

For every service page  Add 2-4 links to area pages    
Add a short “We serve these areas” list at the bottom

For every area page  Add 3-6 links to service pages    
Add a short “Services here” list

For homepage and contact page  Link to all (or most) area pages    
Link to the most important service pages

**Step 5:** Final checks  

Make sure every important page has at least a few incoming links.    
Ask someone to click the links and see if they go to the right page.    
Tell the client: “We added helpful links so customers and Google can find everything easier.”

**Things NOT to do**  
Do not add more than 8-10 links on one page.    
Do not use exactly the same link text many times.    
Do not add links that have nothing to do with the page.    
Do not put all links only in the footer.

That is it. Keep it simple. Add a few helpful links per page. Do this for every service page and every area page. The website will become much stronger for local search.

# Citations

Google is looking for high trust sites to point to you. There’s a couple of great ways to complete your Citation profile 

1) ## The 80/20 of Citations

These are must haves in terms of your client being visible. These need a profile set up and NAP consistent with your website and GBP. 

And you can do them manually, usually have to ask your client to help you with verifying the emails though:

Bing Maps \- [https://www.bing.com/forbusiness/](https://www.bing.com/forbusiness/)   
Apple Business Connect \- [businessconnect.apple.com](http://businessconnect.apple.com)  
FourSquare \- [https://foursquare.com/products/business-listings/](https://foursquare.com/products/business-listings/) (this costs $20)  
Yelp \- [https://biz.yelp.com/claim?utm\_campaign=add\_business\&utm\_content=add\_business\_as\_owner\&utm\_medium=www\&utm\_source=search\_page](https://biz.yelp.com/claim?utm_campaign=add_business&utm_content=add_business_as_owner&utm_medium=www&utm_source=search_page)

(this one mainly for US, I don’t do it for Euro clients:)  
Axle \- [https://local-listings.data-axle.com/why\_local\_listings](https://local-listings.data-axle.com/why_local_listings)  
[https://www.data-axle.com/marketing-solutions/local-listings-management/\#plans](https://www.data-axle.com/marketing-solutions/local-listings-management/#plans)

Do these 4 or 5 and you will have a metric ton of citation work already done.

2) ## Finding highest opportunity and most relevant citations

I want you to do something really simple.

Pick the keyword that you’re trying to rank for. Let’s say it’s “marketing bureau amsterdam”. Now check out the top 20 organic results. So just go down the list and see which websites are ranking.

Notice which of them are directories or lists that you could get a citation on. Example:

![][image26]![][image27]

In this list you have “[sortlist.nl](http://sortlist.nl)” and “[Trustoo.nl](http://Trustoo.nl)”

They are ranking in the top 20 for this term. Which means Google is telling you THESE SITES ARE RELEVANT FOR THIS SEARCH.

Which means it’s probably a really good citation to get. Go to these sites and see how you can sign up. 

You can repeat this for a couple variations of your keyword. 

You can obviously also just ask AI to do the above. It’ll do a good job in finding you potential sources for citations. 

Once you have the 80/20 of citations done AND you’ve found relevant citations based on the above search method you’re well on your way to improving rankings.

Most businesses never take these two steps. So a lot of times you just win by default because no one does these steps.  

### Additional option 1\) Check out competitor’s backlink profiles

If you search the term and check out the competition you’ll obviously see their GBPs.

You can do this for the top 3, top 5, top 10, however far you want to go. It will mostly show you sites that you can rank your clients on because other competitors rank there as well. Just fill in the voids.

You can also prompt AI and let it help you. Like this:

***can you suggest some backlinks I could get for a \<niche\> in \<location\>?***

It will suggest some great options.

# Weekly tings

Weekly updates on page (Generate with AI, lightly edit, blast)  
Weekly pictures with geodata. Can be AI generated, but then printscreen, add geotags. If you’re ranking on the outskirts of a service area, add those geotags to it to rank higher. Check out [https://geosetter.de/en/download-en/](https://geosetter.de/en/download-en/) 

# Client Management

Tell clients to do 2 things:

1) get reviews regularly, make it a point to ask clients regularly, it’s very important that there’s a regular stream of these.   
     
2) send me new pictures of your work, business, whatever so we can upload it. Do it weekly. Can also post weekly on IG / FB and we’ll get it.

# Black Hat vs White Hat

Last point:

We are rendering whitehat services. Meaning \- we follow Google rules. For the simple reason that NOT doing this could get your client’s profile banned. And we don’t want that to happen.

There are a ton of people that do NOT follow these rules. They just blast fake shit AND/OR they rank a fake business just to rent that position out to another real business. Here’s a good example.

![][image31]

Notice how absolutely stuffed to shit the title is for this business. All caps, no real business is named this way. This should make your ears perk up.

But maybe these people were smart and they actually named their business MANCHESTER TREE & STUMP REMOVALS/MANCHESTER TREE SURGEON M4.

Let’s see where they’re located.

![][image32]  
They are in a shopping mall. That is… odd. Tree surgeons usually don’t set up shop in a shopping mall.

Go to the website and the website never mentions an address. Only a phone number.

So we’re probably dealing with someone that built this page, ranked it, then rents it out for a monthly fee to a real service provider.

We appreciate the hustle… but they have to go. Because they’re in the way. It’s not a matter of principle, it’s a matter of practicality. 

So we make a report by clicking the SUGGEST AN EDIT button:

![][image33]a

We pick the “place is closed or not here” and we add a pic of the inside of the shopping mall for illustration. I’ve sent this in, maybe in future reports I’ll also add a pic of a quick explanation, like: “keyword stuffed title, says they are located in a shopping mall but there’s nothing there, clearly a fake business.”

Could also have the client drop by, make a quick video walking by the location, showing it’s non existing, and send that in later if the former approach didn’t work.

Again \- I don’t blame them for trying. They are just in the way. 

Also \- be 100% sure this is not a real business. We’re not trying to fuck real businesses over AND if we report businesses for no viable cause Google will conclude pretty quickly that our opinion sucks and ignore any future reports. 

*(note to self \- check out the blackhatter backlinks)*
